titre: What If Your Eyesight Got 30% Sharper Every Second?
texte:
Your eyesight gets 30% sharper every second. At second 4 you see like an eagle, at second 17 you could spot a person from the space station, at second 28 you beat the Hubble telescope, and at second 55 you can see a black hole. The catch: physics says your pupil would then need to be 2.6 miles wide.
Sources: Webvision (University of Utah); US Mint; Reymond (1985); NASA; FIFA; ESA Hubble; Kervella et al. (2003); ESO; Event Horizon Telescope (2019); OpenStax University Physics.

titre: E se você cortasse uma pizza em 4 a cada segundo?
texte:
Corte uma pizza em 4 a cada segundo e fique com um só pedaço. No corte 8 ele pesa menos que um grão de arroz, no 25 menos que uma bactéria e no 43 seu pedaço é um único átomo. Aí a faca para: em grego, "átomo" quer dizer literalmente "que não pode ser cortado".
Fontes: USDA FoodData Central; BioNumbers (Harvard); Vollmer et al., PNAS (2008); Sigma-Aldrich; CODATA 2018.

titre: What If You Cut a Pizza Into 4 Every Second?
texte:
Cut a pizza into 4 every second and keep only one piece. At cut 8 it weighs less than a grain of rice, at cut 25 less than a bacterium, and at cut 43 your piece is a single atom. That's when the knife has to stop: in Greek, "atom" literally means "uncuttable".
Sources: USDA FoodData Central; BioNumbers (Harvard); Vollmer et al., PNAS (2008); Sigma-Aldrich; CODATA 2018.

texte:
A pepperoncini at 500 SHU gets 40% hotter every second: it beats any jalapeño at second 9, the ghost pepper at second 23, the Pepper X world record at second 26, pure capsaicin at second 31, and at second 52 it reaches the hottest substance known, which doesn't even come from a pepper.
Sources: Guinness World Records, Chile Pepper Institute (NMSU), Winthrop University, Wikipedia (Scoville scale, Resiniferatoxin, Euphorbia resinifera), Discover Magazine.

titre: E se uma bola de neve ficasse 60% mais pesada a cada segundo?
texte:
Uma bola de neve fica 60% mais pesada a cada segundo enquanto desce a montanha: pesa mais que você aos 13 segundos, que uma baleia-azul no segundo 29, que a Torre Eiffel no segundo 38 e que a Grande Pirâmide no segundo 52. Mas uma bola de neve só cresce comendo neve: no fim, ela engoliu 1 metro de neve de 4.800 campos de futebol.
Cálculo: bola compactada a 400 kg/m³ (neve compactada pelo vento), neve no chão a 250 kg/m³.
Fontes: Paterson, The Physics of Glaciers; USBC; Walpole et al., BMC Public Health 2012; Smithsonian's National Zoo; NOAA Fisheries; NASA; toureiffel.paris; arquivos da Harland & Wolff; Guinness World Records; IEEE Spectrum; FIFA.

titre: E se o tempo ficasse duas vezes mais rápido a cada segundo?
texte:
O tempo fica duas vezes mais rápido a cada segundo: um segundo dura uma hora no segundo 12, um ano inteiro no segundo 25, mais que uma vida humana no segundo 32, e no segundo 51 os dinossauros morreram há menos de um segundo. No segundo 59, um único segundo dura mais que a idade do universo.
Fontes: BIPM, ONU World Population Prospects 2024, Smithsonian, NSF, USGS, Planck 2018.

titre: What If a Snowball Got 60% Heavier Every Second?
texte:
A snowball gets 60% heavier every second as it rolls downhill: it outweighs you after 13 seconds, a blue whale at second 29, the Eiffel Tower at second 38 and the Great Pyramid at second 52. But a snowball can only grow by eating snow: by the end it has swallowed 3 feet of snow from 5,300 soccer fields.
Math: snowball packed at 400 kg/m³ (wind-packed snow), snow on the ground at 250 kg/m³.
Sources: Paterson, The Physics of Glaciers; USBC; Walpole et al., BMC Public Health 2012; Smithsonian's National Zoo; NOAA Fisheries; NASA; toureiffel.paris; Harland & Wolff records; Guinness World Records; IEEE Spectrum; FIFA.

titre: E se a água ficasse 3 vezes mais espessa a cada segundo?
texte:
A água fica 3 vezes mais espessa a cada segundo: azeite no segundo 4, mel no segundo 9, piche (uma gota por década) no segundo 24, mais espessa que granito no segundo 48 e, no segundo 51, tão espessa quanto o manto da Terra, que ainda flui sob os seus pés na velocidade em que as suas unhas crescem.

titre: What If Every Domino Was 50% Bigger Than the Last?
texte:
Each domino is 50% bigger than the one before, and one falls every second. Domino 15 is taller than you, domino 30 is taller than the Burj Khalifa, and domino 42 reaches space. The craziest part: a domino really can knock over one 1.5 times its size.
Sources: Whitehead, American Journal of Physics (1983); Stephen Morris, University of Toronto; Guinness World Records; JAXA; FAI; Energy Institute Statistical Review 2024; The Wood Database.

titre: What If a Candle Got 4 Times Stronger Every Second?
texte:
A candle releases 4 times more energy every second. Stronger than a horse at second 2, a dam at second 13, all of humanity at second 19, a hurricane at second 22, and at second 41 it shines like the Sun. The catch: it would burn a Moon's worth of wax every 2.6 hours, about 1.9 billion times more fuel than the real Sun, which runs on nuclear fusion.
Sources: Wikipedia (Candle); NIST; US DOE / LBNL; US Bureau of Reclamation; Energy Institute (2024); NOAA AOML; IAU 2015; Ribas et al. (2017); NASA.

titre: What If a Hydraulic Press Pushed 40% Harder Every Second?
texte:
A hydraulic press pushes 40% harder every second on a block of graphite, the stuff in pencils. Espresso pressure at second 7, steel starts to flow at second 24, diamond-making pressure at second 33, and at second 45 it matches the center of the Earth. The twist: labs reach that pressure every day with two tiny diamonds and the force of a 25 lb weight.
Sources: NIST; Specialty Coffee Association; ASTM A36; GIA Gems & Gemology; Scientific Reports (2018); PREM; Nature (2008); O'Bannon et al. (2018).

titre: What If Your Heart Beat 12% Faster Every Second?
texte:
Your heart beats 12% faster every second, starting at a calm 60 bpm: past a 20-year-old's maximum heart rate at second 11, faster than a mouse at second 21, and at second 27 it beats so fast you can hear it as a hum. Then it outruns a shrew, a hummingbird's wings and a bumblebee, until it plays the exact note an orchestra tunes to.
Sources: Harvard Health Publishing, Journal of Experimental Biology (Etruscan shrew), Chesapeake Bay Program, Arnold Arboretum of Harvard University, ISO 16.

titre: What If You Jumped Twice as High Every Second?
texte:
Start at half a meter and double it every second: you beat the 2.45 m world record (Sotomayor, 1993) at 3 s, the Eiffel Tower at 10 s and reach space (100 km, Kármán line) at 18 s.
But taking off at v = √(2gh) ≈ 1.6 km/s (Mach 4.7), the air ahead is stopped against you: T₀ = T + v²/2cp ≈ 1,294 °C, hotter than basalt lava (~1,200 °C, USGS).

titre: What If You Grew 10% Taller Every Second?
texte:
At 1.1ⁿ you pass a giraffe at 13 s, the Statue of Liberty (93 m, NPS) at 42 s and the Eiffel Tower (330 m) at 55 s. Square-cube law: bone area grows ×k², weight ×k³.
At 58 s you're 440 m tall: each femur (394 mm² of cortical bone ×k²) carries 557,693 t, a stress of 219 MPa, above bone's 205 MPa compressive strength.

titre: What If Your Sneeze Got Twice as Strong Every Second?
texte:
A real sneeze moves at only 4.5 m/s (Tang et al., PLoS ONE 2013), not 100 mph. Doubling every second: a hurricane at 3 s, faster than an EF5 tornado at 5 s, than sound at 7 s, than a rifle bullet (960 m/s) at 8 s.
Newton's third law: the jet pushes you back with F = ρAv² (mouth ~4 cm², Gupta 2009). At 9 s that's 2,548 N, 3.7× the weight of a 70 kg person.

titre: What If Your Hair Grew Twice as Long Every Second?
texte:
Starting at 5 cm and doubling every second, your hair passes a bus at 8 s and an Olympic pool at 10 s. 100,000 hairs of 70 µm (density 1.32 g/cm³) weigh 0.5 kg per meter: at 12 s, 205 m of hair weighs 104 kg, more than you.

titre: What If a Skyscraper Doubled Its Floors Every Second?
texte:
One floor (3.9 m), doubling every second: past the Empire State at 7 s (128 floors), the Burj Khalifa at 8 s, 1,024 floors and 4 km at 10 s. Even solid steel (yield 250 MPa, 7,850 kg/m³) crushes under its own weight past σ/(ρg) ≈ 3.2 km.
Sources: CTBUH Skyscraper Center (Empire State, Burj Khalifa), CTBUH height calculator (3.9 m per floor), ASTM A36 steel.

titre: What If You Ate Twice as Much Every Second?
texte:
One plate (0.5 kg), doubling every second: more than your own weight at 8 s, an elephant at 14 s, a blue whale at 19 s. Each second beats all the seconds before combined: at 36 s one second is a day of the world's harvest, at 45 s a whole year (9.6 billion tonnes of crops, FAO 2022).
Sources: FAO FAOSTAT (crop production 2022), NOAA Fisheries (blue whale), San Diego Zoo (elephant).

titre: What If You Shrank by Half Every Second?
texte:
From 1.75 m, halving every second: mouse size at 4 s, smaller than an ant at 9 s, than a red blood cell at 18 s. But your 3 mm pupil shrinks too, and diffraction blurs light through a small opening: legally blind at 4 s, and at 13 s your pupil (366 nm) is smaller than any visible light (380-700 nm).
Sources: NASA (visible spectrum), StatPearls/NCBI (pupil size), Harvard BioNumbers (red blood cell), SSA (legal blindness), AntWiki (Lasius niger).

titre: What If Your Phone Battery Doubled Its Charge Every Second?
texte:
A full phone battery holds about 13 Wh (iPhone 15: 12.98 Wh). Doubling every second: 3,200% at 5 s, more energy than a kilo of TNT (4.184 MJ) at 7 s, more than a 50 L tank of gas (34.2 MJ/L) at 16 s. Overfilled lithium cells go into thermal runaway past 300 °C.
Sources: iPhone 15 regulatory filing (MacRumors), NIST TNT equivalent, UL Research Institutes (thermal runaway).
